**Reasoning:** The dark gray-black dusty/granular coating on the stem junction with white mycelium visible inside the crack is most consistent with **Gray Mold (Botrytis cinerea)**. Botrytis characteristically produces gray sporulation masses (conidiophores + conidia) on wounded or stressed stem tissue, especially at nodes and junctions, which appears dark gray to nearly black. The orange-brown discoloration beneath is consistent with Botrytis-induced stem lesions, and the visible white areas represent underlying mycelium.
